contracts.title: GET/HEAD discovery
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented (2026-10-13): no HEAD. One GET with `Range: bytes=OFFSET-` both verifies range support and supplies data; the validated 206 body is adopted by the segment starting at OFFSET (a resume probes from the first missing byte). A 200 body is streamed directly. Only a malformed 206 or 416 triggers one further full GET. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) counts requests: one request for a one-connection file and for no-range servers.

contracts.title: HTTP methods and request bodies
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: `Options.method/body` and CLI `--method/--data-file` replay the method and a bounded (1 MiB) body on every probe/range request; GET with body, HEAD/CONNECT/TRACE/OPTIONS are rejected; 301/302/303 on a non-GET request fails instead of becoming GET, 307/308 preserve it. Context hash covers method/body. Fixture verifies POST-only file with 4 connections, 307 and refused 302. Daemon IPC `submit_request` carries method/body (tested in [request_context.py](../tests/integration/request_context.py): POST replay with correct hash, GET refusal, method/body validation, restart persistence, CLI `submit-post`, persisted proxy routing). Browser submissions do not yet carry method/body.

contracts.title: One-shot and expiring URLs
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: request adoption means a ranged or full one-shot link is fetched by the probe response alone. If extra range connections are refused (401/403/404/410 on their first request), those ranges are released and the adopted open-ended stream absorbs adjacent untouched ranges; fixture `oneshot.bin` (8 connections) and `oneshot-norange.bin` succeed with one accepted request. No request-token lease, expiry detection or site rules. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies oneshot and oneshot-norange with 8 connections.

contracts.title: Range capability and boundaries
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented static path: strict Content-Range parser, bounded segments, identity encoding, exact body coverage. Accept-Ranges alone is not used as proof. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies 8-connection ranged download, 1-connection single request, and range header parsing. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N04_range_boundaries` passes.

contracts.title: Ignored or malformed partial response
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: Malformed probe falls back to full transfer; a server that stops honoring ranges during a segmented transfer triggers a typed `RangeUnreliable` error (at offset + reason), stops all workers, and parks the task in `restart_required` with a recorded `restart_reason`, keeping the partial data. `TaskRestart` (IPC/CLI) deletes only that task's `.part` and `.part.meta` and requeues it from byte zero. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies wrong-range handling and RangeUnreliable; [restart_required.py](../tests/integration/restart_required.py) verifies restart_required parking, retry suppression, and TaskRestart from byte zero. Suspect bytes are not isolated.

contracts.title: Representation compression
contracts.current_behavior: Restricted: sends Accept-Encoding identity and rejects nonidentity final/range responses. Cargo has no reqwest compression feature.

contracts.title: Known and unknown response length
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: unknown size streams the adopted full response until EOF with total/ETA unknown; a length-less stream that ends at EOF completes with `size_unverified` set and a notice that the file might be incomplete; zero-length resources (416 to the open range) complete as empty files; no resumable metadata for non-range content. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies empty body (416) and flaky non-range retry from zero. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N07_response_length` passes. [Engine gaps](../tests/integration/engine_gaps.py) verifies the unknown-length EOF flag and notice; `crates/xdm-http` unit test `unknown_length_eof_is_flagged_unverified` covers the engine flag.

contracts.title: Redirect chains and credentials
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: maximum ten hops; Referer is not rewritten on redirect. Cookie/Authorization/UA/Referer/Accept(-Language) may follow cross-origin redirects because the client strips Cookie/Authorization on host change (fixture verifies the redirected host receives no Cookie); any other custom header stops cross-origin redirects, and any supplied header stops an HTTPS→HTTP downgrade. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies cross-host redirect strips Cookie, same-origin preserves headers.

contracts.title: Cookie/User-Agent/Referer/header forwarding
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: HTTP header list is persisted and shared among workers; engine owns Range/If-Range/Host/encoding/length framing. No browser-context cookie refresh. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies custom headers (User-Agent) sent and Cookie stripped on cross-host redirect. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N09_header_forwarding` passes.

contracts.title: Origin/path login credentials
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented on Linux (2026-10-13): site/path credential store with pattern matching (exact host, wildcard subdomain, path prefix, port), most-specific-first selection, stored in an owner-only (0600) file on Unix — permission-protected, not encrypted — and DPAPI-sealed on Windows (compile-checked only, not run on Windows), never exposed in IPC/exports/logs. Basic auth applied automatically on 401 challenge; task enters `auth_required` with realm, no retry loop; `TaskProvideLogin` IPC requeues with credentials; `--remember` persists origin pattern. Fixture verifies challenge→auth_required, foreign-host login never sent, save/list without passwords, automatic application, wrong password rejected, disabled logins skipped, stdin password entry, credentials.json mode 0600. [Daemon unit tests](../crates/xdm-daemon/src/credentials.rs), [integration fixture](../tests/integration/credentials.py).

contracts.title: Authentication retries and expiry
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): 401 challenge produces `auth_required` status with realm, no automatic retry (queue retry policy excludes 401/407); Basic auth implemented via credential store (N10); `TaskProvideLogin` IPC accepts credentials (file or stdin) and requeues; wrong credentials recorded as `auth_required` again, not failed. No Digest/NTLM negotiation, no password-expiry workflow, no proxy auth (407). [Integration fixture](../tests/integration/credentials.py) covers challenge→auth_required, requeue, wrong password, disabled entry, stdin, secret handling.

contracts.title: Remote-object validators
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: checks size/final URL/header-context hash and available strong ETag/date; ranges send If-Range. Missing response validators are not themselves rejected. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies changed validator detection (identity changed) and ETag handling. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N12_validator_change_rejects_resume` passes.

contracts.title: Ignore modification-time preference
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented: `ResumePolicy { ignore_modification_date: true }` (set per task through `submit_ex` and persisted in the daemon database) lets a resume ignore a changed `Last-Modified` only when the saved length, effective URL and a strong `ETag` all still match. A changed strong ETag or length always refuses. Without a strong ETag (absent or weak) the modification date stays binding. Refusal parks the task in `restart_required` instead of splicing bytes. Verified in `crates/xdm-http` unit tests and [naming_duplicates.py](../tests/integration/naming_duplicates.py) (ignore-date resume completes with matching ETag; default policy and changed ETag park in restart_required).

contracts.title: User-visible filename/type changes
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: Resolves server-chosen filenames from `Content-Disposition` (RFC 6266 parameters; RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''` takes precedence over `filename`), falling back to the redirected final URL's last path segment. Names are sanitized: path separators stripped, control and Windows-invalid characters replaced with `_`, trailing dots and spaces removed, and reserved device names such as CON or com1 disambiguated (`CON_`, `com1_.bin`). For server-named tasks, a missing extension or a dynamic-page extension (`.php`, `.asp`, `.html`, ...) is replaced from a known Content-Type (`getfile.php` served as application/zip becomes `.zip`); a real extension is never rewritten. A text/html answer for a binary-named target fails the single-stream task with "server returned an HTML page instead of a file" and no retry; a binary labelled text/html whose body is not HTML still downloads. Segmented transfers do not run this HTML check. An occupied server-chosen name receives a ` (2)`-style suffix instead of overwriting. Direct `submit_ex` submissions refuse a normalized duplicate URL with the owning task ID unless `allow_duplicate` is set; legacy submissions keep the old behavior. No consent prompt exists. Verified in [naming_duplicates.py](../tests/integration/naming_duplicates.py) (UTF-8 disposition, redirect-renamed file, reserved names, collision suffix, duplicate refusal), [engine_gaps.py](../tests/integration/engine_gaps.py) (MIME extension reconciliation, HTML-page failure with zero retries, labelled binary download, collision with a foreign partial) and `crates/xdm-http` unit tests (filename parsing and sanitization, MIME reconciliation, HTML sniffing and guard).

contracts.title: Permission/permanent HTTP errors
contracts.current_behavior: Partial:403/404 nonretryable; daemon records failed. Error is text rather than typed recovery classification. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) and [CLI fixture](../tests/integration/cli_http.py) verify 403 handling and no completed file. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N15_permanent_http_errors` passes.

contracts.title: Transient server/network retries
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: probe/full requests retry up to four times on network/408/429/5xx honoring Retry-After (capped 30 s) with pause-aware waits; range requests retry the same way. Full non-range streams now retry from byte zero after a disconnect or short body (fixture `flaky-norange.bin`). No jitter or global retry fairness. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) and [CLI fixture](../tests/integration/cli_http.py) verify 503 retry and flaky non-range retry from zero. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N16_transient_retries` passes.

contracts.title: Timeouts, DNS and diagnostics
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: blocking client has30-second request timeout; network errors propagate. No separate DNS/connect/read-idle limits or structured diagnostics. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N17_timeouts_and_refusals` exercises refusal, NXDOMAIN, and stalled-server timeout.

contracts.title: TLS/certificates and Microsoft TLS1.3 preference
contracts.current_behavior: Different backend: reqwest rustls-tls. No Microsoft TLS toggle, custom trust/client certificates or detailed certificate UI. Actual protocol/cipher coverage not audited.

contracts.title: FTP authentication/control replies
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): independent FTP client (`xdm-ftp` crate) implements control channel subset for resumable single-stream download: USER/PASS (anonymous or credentials from URL), TYPE I, SIZE, MDTM, EPSV with PASV fallback, REST, RETR, QUIT. Multiline replies parsed with bounded continuation lines (128). Passive data connections always made to control peer (defeats FTP bounce). Credentials from `ftp://user:pass@host/path` URL. No active mode (PORT/EPRT). Daemon tasks accept `ftp://` URLs with progress/pause/resume via IPC. [Crate unit tests](../crates/xdm-ftp/src/lib.rs), [crate integration tests](../crates/xdm-ftp/tests/ftp.rs), [daemon IPC fixture](../tests/integration/protocol_tasks.py) covers submit, live progress, pause/resume, hash verification.

contracts.title: FTP passive and active data modes
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): passive mode implemented via EPSV (preferred) with PASV fallback. PASV advertised address is ignored; data connection always made to control peer IP (security). EPSV/PASV reply parsing bounded. Active mode (PORT/EPRT) NOT implemented. Single serialized control session per task; no concurrent data connections. [Crate tests](../crates/xdm-ftp/tests/ftp.rs) verify EPSV, PASV, foreign PASV IP uses control peer, multiline banner.

contracts.title: FTP REST/SIZE and resume
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): SIZE, MDTM, REST implemented. Resume guarded by SIZE+MDTM validators in `.part.ftp` checkpoint; mismatch requires explicit restart (`--restart` or new task). Checkpoint stores size and modification time; on resume, REST sent only if validators match. Rejected REST, changed MDTM, changed SIZE all require restart (fixtures verify). No-clobber publish (hard link + remove, checked rename fallback). [Crate tests](../crates/xdm-ftp/tests/ftp.rs): disconnect→resume, changed MDTM requires restart, changed SIZE requires restart, rejected REST requires restart, PASV foreign IP uses control peer. [Daemon IPC fixture](../tests/integration/protocol_tasks.py): submit, live progress, pause/resume, hash.

contracts.title: FTP optional connections/pipelining
contracts.current_behavior: Missing: single serialized control session per task; no concurrent data connections, no command pipelining. Per-host FTP session budget and cross-task synchronization not implemented.

contracts.title: Manual per-protocol proxy
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): engine `Proxy::Manual` takes separate proxy URLs for http and https targets (HTTP proxy, HTTPS CONNECT, credentials in URL user info); CLI `--proxy`. Fixture routes a 4-connection transfer through a logging forward proxy. No daemon/GUI settings model, no FTP proxy, no 407 prompt. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) and [request_context fixture](../tests/integration/request_context.py) verify HTTP proxy, HTTPS CONNECT, and persisted manual proxy routing.

contracts.title: SOCKS4/SOCKS5 and remote DNS
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): reqwest `socks` feature enabled; `socks4://`, `socks5://` and `socks5h://` (proxy-side DNS) URLs with user/password. Fixture verifies SOCKS5 user/password auth, domain-type CONNECT for socks5h and failure on wrong credentials. No settings UI. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies SOCKS5 auth, socks5h domain-type CONNECT, and wrong credential rejection.

contracts.title: Proxy exclusions and host patterns
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): manual proxies take a bypass list of host names (subdomain match), IPs and CIDR ranges via reqwest NoProxy; fixture verifies a bypassed host connects directly. Wildcard/port-specific patterns are not supported. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies bypass list (127.0.0.1 bypassed) and direct connection for bypassed hosts.

contracts.title: System proxy/PAC/WPAD
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: `Proxy::System` uses proxy environment variables only (fixture verifies they are honored and that `--no-proxy` ignores them). No OS settings import, PAC evaluation or WPAD.

contracts.title: Browser proxy/VPN context fallback
contracts.current_behavior: Missing: captured task has no resolved browser proxy route.

contracts.title: Windows dial-up/VPN and redial
contracts.current_behavior: Missing.

contracts.title: Static segment allocation
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented independent static1–16 partitioning; one worker thread per segment,64KiB per-worker read buffer. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies 1-connection and 8-connection downloads with correct hashes. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N29_static_segments` passes.

contracts.title: Dynamic splitting and worker reuse
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): workers form a pool of the requested size that claims idle segments; when none remain a worker splits the largest unclaimed remainder (≥1 MiB) of a running segment at its midpoint, with per-chunk reservations so split points never overlap in-flight bytes. Splits are checkpointed. Thresholds are independent; no stall-based reassignment. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies 8-connection download with correct hash (dynamic splitting exercised).

contracts.title: Stall recovery and adaptive connections
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented: Configurable stall timeout (default 15 s, valid 1–600 s) aborts a connection that delivers no bytes, reopens from the worker's cursor, and counts toward the retry budget. The stall-timeout setting is persisted in the daemon database across restarts, adjustable via CLI / IPC (GetStallTimeout, SetStallTimeout), and available on direct CLI downloads via `--stall-timeout`. Rate-limited throttling is distinguished from stalls. Verified in [engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) and [restart_required.py](../tests/integration/restart_required.py).

contracts.title: Overlap/data-corruption validation
contracts.current_behavior: Partial safety: strict headers/body lengths/validators; no persisted interval checksums or byte-overlap comparison.

contracts.title: Preallocation and offset writes
contracts.current_behavior: Independent implementation: set_len plus positional write_at; not explicit Linux fallocate or privileged Windows SetFileValidData.

contracts.title: Checkpoint schema and write ordering
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: version2 JSON .part.meta, per-segment cursor, URLs/context hash/validators; data sync then temporary metadata sync then rename. Directory sync and Windows existing-destination rename semantics require tests. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N34_checkpoint_write_ordering` passes (SIGKILL never yields a torn checkpoint; metadata stays usable and every resumed transfer verifies exact hash).

contracts.title: Pause/resume with one connection
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented (2026-10-13): connections=1 uses a single range worker with a `.part.meta` checkpoint. Saved segments are resumed by any worker count (excess segments are processed in turn, spare workers split). Fixture pauses and resumes 1→1, 1→4 and 4→1 with hash checks and verifies the resume probe starts at the saved byte. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies pause/resume 1→1, 1→4, 4→1 with hash checks.

contracts.title: Non-range pause/restart
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: Single-stream non-range pause retains .part without metadata; next attempt restarts at zero. Tasks encountering corrupted or non-resumable streams park in `restart_required` with an explicit reason, preventing retry loops until restarted via `TaskRestart` IPC/CLI (which deletes partial data and restarts from byte zero). Disconnects during a full stream retry from zero are bounded by queue retry policy. Verified in [engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) and [restart_required.py](../tests/integration/restart_required.py).

contracts.title: Crash recovery and stale running states
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: daemon maps running/pausing→queued at open; segmented checkpoint validation resumes. Power-loss durability and repeated Windows checkpoint replacement not proven. [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N37_crash_recovery` passes (SIGKILL during active transfer, daemon restart maps stale running→queued, resume verifies exact hash).

contracts.title: Separate temporary and final directories
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: HTTP tasks keep `.part` and `.part.meta` in an optional absolute temp directory (stored canonically per task; a task keeps the location it started with; a fresh HTTP task adopts the setting only when no partials sit beside its destination). When the temp directory is on another device, completion copies to the destination with a space preflight and no-replace publish. FTP partials still sit beside the destination; there is no per-user default temp root and no verified handling of removable or missing volumes. Verified in [engine_gaps.py](../tests/integration/engine_gaps.py) (same-volume and /dev/shm cross-volume publish, pause and resume, delete_partial, PartialScan and delete inside the temp directory) and `crates/xdm-http` unit tests (`segmented_download_uses_temp_dir_and_sets_server_time`, `temp_partials_are_distinct_per_destination`, `copy_publish_installs_without_clobbering_and_keeps_part_on_conflict`).

contracts.title: Disk-full and access-denied assembly
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): disk-space preflight via `fstatvfs` and rollback of failed `fallocate`; `SIGXFSZ` ignored with actionable `EFBIG`/`ENOSPC` errors surfaced to the caller. Permission-denied destinations fail cleanly. Full-filesystem injection requires a size-limited mount (not available unprivileged); this half remains xfail in the contract suite while xdm-http unit tests cover the preflight and error reporting. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) covers permission denial; [contracts_core.py](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N39_disk_full_and_access_denied` is xfail.

contracts.title: Large files and filesystem limits
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented (2026-10-13): u64 offsets/lengths and set_len; >4 GiB crossing verified with exact last-byte checks and no usize truncation. Filesystem size-limit preflight via `RLIMIT_FSIZE` surfaces an actionable diagnostic instead of a signal kill. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) crosses 4 GiB; [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N40_large_files` passes.

contracts.title: File timestamps
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: HTTP completed files take their modification time from a valid `Last-Modified` header, set on the open file handle before publish, including resumed downloads. `preserve_server_time=false` opts out (CLI sets it true); an unparseable date leaves the time unchanged. No creation-time (birth time) handling and no per-platform policy; FTP files are not stamped. Verified in [engine_gaps.py](../tests/integration/engine_gaps.py) (Last-Modified applied, opt-out, invalid date unchanged, resumed download) and `crates/xdm-http` unit tests (`http_dates_parse_and_garbage_is_rejected`, `server_time_changes_only_for_valid_dates`, `single_stream_download_keeps_time_unchanged_when_disabled`, `segmented_download_uses_temp_dir_and_sets_server_time`).

contracts.title: Finalize, rename and output conflicts
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): publication uses a hard link plus removal of `.part` (checked rename when hard links are unsupported), so a destination created during the transfer is never replaced; the error keeps the completed `.part`. Fixture creates the destination mid-transfer and verifies both files. Cross-volume move remains absent. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) verifies no-clobber publication (destination created mid-transfer). [Core contracts](../tests/integration/contracts_core.py) `test_N42_finalize_no_clobber` passes.

contracts.title: Orphan partial cleanup
contracts.current_behavior: Missing: stopped-task remove retains files by design; no orphan inventory/cleanup.

contracts.title: Default/per-server connection caps
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: per-task 1–16 connections and daemon job cap 1–16. HTTP engine per-host connection budgets (`daemon host-connections PATTERN N` or `remove`, 1–256; default 16 per host) are enforced by leases shared by all HTTP tasks and persisted; an exact host name wins over the longest `*.domain` pattern (unit tests leases_never_exceed_the_budget_and_release_on_drop and host_patterns_prefer_exact_then_longest_wildcard). [Bandwidth fixture](../tests/integration/bandwidth.py) peaks above 3 connections to one host without a budget and between 1 and 3 with budget 3. Budgets key on the submitted host name only; redirect host changes, a connection profile setting and FTP (not governed) are not covered; untested on Windows.

contracts.title: Per-file limiter and remembered exceptions
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: a shared token bucket across all of a task's workers, persisted task cap, adjustable live. Per-task caps compose with the N46 global and per-host caps; [Bandwidth fixture](../tests/integration/bandwidth.py) checks that a task limited to 6 MiB/s keeps at least 4 MiB/s while another host name is capped at 1 MiB/s. No app default enabled-state or per-file exception inheritance policy. [Task rate fixture](../tests/integration/task_rate.py) verifies live cap changes, counters/ETA, persisted cap, pause/resume, unlimited resume, and exact output hash.

contracts.title: Aggregate/per-host bandwidth limits
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: a global cap (`daemon limit-global KIB` or `unlimited`, 1 KiB/s to 4 GiB/s) is split equally among active HTTP tasks (unit test active_consumers_split_the_rate_equally) and changes live; per-host caps (`daemon limit-host PATTERN KIB`, `unlimited` or `remove`; host name, `*.domain` or `*`) are persisted and change live. [Bandwidth fixture](../tests/integration/bandwidth.py) uses a loopback server and a dedicated test daemon: two tasks stay at or below 4.4 MiB/s total with each at least 1.5 MiB/s; a live raise to 8 MiB/s takes effect; a capped host name stays at or below 1.25 MiB/s while another host name stays above 4 MiB/s; removing the limit restores speed; output hashes match. Limits: equal split only, no priority weighting; per-host caps use the submitted host name (localhost and 127.0.0.1 are different names); HTTP engine only; untested on Windows.

contracts.title: Usage quota and automatic resumption
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: fixed-window usage quota (`daemon quota MIB HOURS` or `off`). The window opens when the first HTTP transfer runs after the previous window ended and lasts the set time; payload bytes of every HTTP task in every queue count, and a transfer can overshoot by one read per connection. At the limit active tasks move to quota_wait and resume automatically when the window closes; the used-byte ledger and window start persist across daemon restart. [Bandwidth fixture](../tests/integration/bandwidth.py) verifies that a 6 MiB quota over a 7.2 s window pauses a 10 MiB task with 6 to 8 MiB used, that the state and ledger survive a restart, that the task resumes after the window, and that the hash matches. Limits: fixed window, not rolling; payload bytes only; no warning before the limit; no clock-change test; untested on Windows.

contracts.title: Resource efficiency contract
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: bounded 64 KiB buffers, task-limit bounded threads; per-MiB sync checkpoint and blocking worker design measured (2026-10-13). Daemon idle: ~7 MiB RSS with 0% CPU over 30 s including 1000 queued tasks. CLI downloads: 256 MiB at 1–16 connections achieves 183–532 MiB/s, peak RSS 5.7–26 MiB. Benchmark script [bench/run_bench.py](../bench/run_bench.py) samples `/proc` tree at 100 ms intervals, verifies hash integrity. Not yet compared to other download managers; Windows measurements absent.

contracts.title: Queue types and default queues
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: Main plus named ordinary queues. A synchronization queue is created with `daemon queue create NAME [LIMIT] --sync` and its type is stored, but there is no default synchronization queue and no mode switch to change a queue's type later. Ordinary queues reject check and sync-interval; a completed task assigned to a synchronization queue stays there as a member. [Daemon IPC fixture](../tests/integration/daemon_ipc.py) verifies queue creation, durable acceptance, and ordering/concurrency; [Sync queues fixture](../tests/integration/sync_queues.py) verifies --sync creation, rejection of misuse on ordinary queues, and that a queue holding completed members cannot be removed. Migration of existing queues is not covered; untested on Windows.

contracts.title: Named queues and membership
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: create/rename/empty-remove/atomic stopped-task assign; Main fixed, max32, names1–64bytes. Every task always has queue_id1 by default; no no-queue option or queue selector in all creation paths. [Named queue fixture](../tests/integration/named_queues.py) verifies separate caps, isolated stop, atomic guarded membership, persisted names/state, and output hashes.

contracts.title: Independent start/stop and global controls
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: `queue start-one ID` sets a per-queue independent-start flag so the queue runs while the global gate is stopped and without starting Main; `queue stop-one`/legacy `disable` clear it; global `queue stop` (and global scheduled start/stop) clears every independent start and interrupts all workers. Legacy `queue enable` still needs the global gate. No GUI gate indicator yet. **Scheduler fixes (2026-10-13):** arming a future timed start (`queue at`) no longer stops running downloads; the timer is armed and active transfers continue. Tested in [scheduler.py](../tests/integration/scheduler.py) and `queue_policies.py`; original semantics remain unverified.

contracts.title: Per-queue simultaneous files
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented bounded per-queue1–16 plus global1–16; Main initial queue limit16/global2 differs observed original default4. [Named queue fixture](../tests/integration/named_queues.py) verifies per-queue and global limits with hash/isolation tests.

contracts.title: Manual queue order and priority
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: `position` column (migrated; new tasks append via trigger), `daemon move ID up

contracts.title: Completion leaves ordinary queue
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: when a task completes, `queue_id` becomes 0 (no live queue) and the origin is kept in `history_queue_id`; queue summary `complete` counts history; a queue with only completed history can be deleted (history is nulled). Existing databases are migrated. Assigning a completed task changes only its history. No synchronization queue exists, so every queue is ordinary. Unit and integration tested.

contracts.title: Queue retry count and rotation
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: per-queue `queue retry ID COUNT

contracts.title: One-time start/stop

contracts.title: Daily/weekday recurrence

contracts.title: Synchronization repeat/check changed objects
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: each completed member of a synchronization queue is checked by `daemon queue check ID` or on an interval (`daemon queue sync-interval ID HOURS MINUTES` or `off`). Interval checks are persisted and the scheduler sleeps until the next due time (unit test pump_reports_none_without_sync_queues_and_remaining_time_otherwise). Each check sends a HEAD with If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since from the saved validators (GET Range 0-0 if HEAD is refused). A 304, or validators that match, downloads nothing; a change is decided by ETag first, then Last-Modified, then length. A changed member is fetched into a temporary file and renamed over the old one; a failed refresh keeps the old file and removes the temporary. Each member gets a sync_updated, sync_unchanged or sync_failed event, and each check a sync_checked summary. [Sync queues fixture](../tests/integration/sync_queues.py) verifies that a first check with matching local size stores the baseline without a GET, that unchanged checks issue HEAD without GET, that a changed ETag is replaced with the new hash, that a 500 or 503 source keeps the old file with no temporary left, that the pending version is picked up after recovery, and that periodic checks run. Gaps: no validator baseline at completion (until the first check only local size is compared); HTTP(S) GET members only; untested on Windows, where rename-over-existing is not exercised.

contracts.title: Completion success/failure/manual-stop rules
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): per-queue cycle state (`idle/running/completed/completed_with_failures/stopped`) with one event per execution (`queue events ID`). Success runs the configured completion action through an injectable adapter: the real OS adapter by default, a recording adapter under `XDM_FAKE_OS_ACTIONS=1` so tests never touch the OS. Settable actions: none, notify, sleep, hibernate, shutdown, restart, exit and program (path plus literal argument list). Failures, manual stop (including global stop) and schedule cutoff record the event with action `suppressed`; an empty start produces no event; new work after completion starts a new cycle; an edited or canceled countdown records `cancelled`. Destructive actions additionally require the per-queue `--confirm-destructive` opt-in and their countdown (Q17). The [completion fixture](../tests/integration/completion_actions.py) with the recording adapter covers notify recorded, unconfirmed shutdown rejected, countdown visible then recorded, cancel prevents and manual stop suppresses; daemon unit tests cover empty-start, new-cycle, final-failure and daemon-restart suppression.

contracts.title: Completion program/file launch
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented (2026-10-13): `queue completion ID program PATH [ARGS...]` stores the executable plus a literal argument list (IPC `CompletionAction::Program`, at most 64 arguments) and launches it without a shell after a qualifying completion, spawned without blocking the daemon while a reaper thread collects the exit status; the queue event records `started`, `executed` or the spawn error. The path is configured per queue, never browser-supplied. The completion fixture launches a real script through the recording adapter and asserts every argument arrives literally, spaces and shell metacharacters (`a;b

contracts.title: Disconnect modem/VPN and app exit
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: the modem/VPN disconnect action remains missing (no dial-up or VPN adapter and no connection scoping). The application-exit action exists: `queue completion ID exit` ends the daemon about 300 ms after the queue completion event so the event insert and reply frame are written first; it needs no destructive opt-in, its configuration is unit-tested, and the recording adapter logs it instead of exiting, so no fixture terminates the daemon.

contracts.title: Shutdown/restart/sleep/hibernate
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented (2026-10-13): sleep, hibernate, shutdown and restart are settable per queue but require explicit opt-in (`--confirm-destructive`, otherwise the command is rejected) plus a persistent cancelable countdown (default 60 s; the daemon accepts 1..86400 s). During the countdown the event reads `pending`, `CompletionStatus` reports queue, action and `seconds_remaining`, and `CompletionCancel` cancels it (`cancelled`); a manual stop, final failure, new cycle, action edit or daemon restart suppresses it without executing. The real adapter spawns commands directly with no shell: Linux uses `notify-send` for notify and `systemctl suspend`/`hibernate`/`poweroff`/`reboot`; the Windows path (PowerShell toast with `msg` fallback, `rundll32 powrprof.dll,SetSuspendState`, `shutdown` `/h` `/s` `/r`) is compile-structural only and untested on Windows. Tests run with `XDM_FAKE_OS_ACTIONS=1` recording adapter: the [completion fixture](../tests/integration/completion_actions.py) verifies notify recorded, unconfirmed shutdown rejected, countdown visible then recorded, cancel prevents and manual stop suppresses, and a daemon unit test proves the real adapter never executes an unarmed power action. File, queue and project completion actions remain absent.

contracts.current_behavior: Implemented: Tracks redirects via webRequest.onBeforeRedirect. Each hop keeps the original Referer, page context and method association; 307/308 keep POST and its form body, while 301/302 on POST and 303 become GET and replay no body (the extension never turns a POST into a GET on its own: a POST whose redirect chain was not observed stays in the browser). The final URL (`finalUrl`) is what is submitted, cookies are read for the final origin only, and only User-Agent, Referer and Content-Type are forwarded, so Authorization and Cookie request headers from earlier hops are dropped. Chain context lives in memory with a 60 s TTL, so it is lost if the background worker restarts mid-chain. Verified with mocked browser APIs only, not a real browser.
